analysis.title: Mind on the Market (Chart of the Week: semiconductor drawdown vs S&P 500)
key_insights: Global semiconductors were nearly 30% below their previous peak on November 6 (trough November 5), approaching the size of the sector's 2025 drawdown, which recovered in 65 days.
The S&P 500's maximum decline during the semiconductor selloff was about 6%, well below the drawdowns that accompanied earlier semiconductor corrections.
The S&P 500 has had four drawdowns over 3% in 2026, including the current one. The average drawdown this year is 1.5% and the maximum is 8.9%.

Drawdown 1 (1/28 to 4/15, trough -8.89% on 3/30, 77 days) was driven by escalating conflict with Iran and higher oil prices. It was a global, broad risk-off move. Energy was the exception, and gold was weak.

Drawdown 2 (June, trough -4.46%) came from renewed Iran tensions, inflation concerns and a repricing of technology valuations. Investors rotated to defensive areas, and infrastructure and higher-quality bonds held up.

Drawdown 3 (August to September, trough -3.03%) came with rising Treasury yields, expectations of a Fed rate hike and concerns over AI investment financing. Higher yields reduced the diversification benefit of bonds, while infrastructure and defensive equity sectors held up.

The current drawdown (from 10/7, trough -5.90% on 11/5, ongoing as of 11/6) is largely a sharp unwind of AI-related trades after the midterm elections. Investors reassessed data-center development given possible regulatory and political constraints. Crowded positioning and de-risking by leveraged and systematic investors amplified it.

Through the market trough, information technology fell 16.9% and communication services fell 14.4%, with steeper losses in parts of the AI ecosystem. Consumer staples rose 12.2%, health care 9.5%, real estate 8.7% and financials 7.1%, which limited the index decline. Bonds, TIPS and infrastructure also provided protection.

State Street remains constructive on the longer-term AI demand story. It argues a slower data-center buildout could push hyperscalers toward their highest-return projects and better utilization, and that the correction reflects uncertainty about timing and economics rather than a collapse in demand.

sector_views.rationale: Fell 16.9% through the current drawdown trough on the AI-trade unwind, but the firm stays constructive on long-term AI demand and sees opportunity to add where conviction holds.
Rose 12.2% through the current drawdown trough, the best sector, as defensive exposure offset AI weakness.
Rose 9.5% through the current drawdown trough, offsetting AI-complex weakness.

tension_points.bull_case: A more measured buildout could push hyperscalers to prioritize their highest-return projects, improve utilization of existing infrastructure and show clearer paths to monetization, strengthening capital efficiency. The correction reflects uncertainty about timing and economics, not collapsing demand.
tension_points.bear_case: Post-midterm regulatory and political constraints could slow data-center development, and questions remain about the pace of investment further out. Crowded positioning amplified the selloff.
